summary.text: 明 means “bright” or “clear.” Early writing includes a sun-and-moon form linked with brightness or dawn, alongside 朙, in which moon and window were interpreted as moonlight entering a room.

formation.text: The record preserves distinct early constructions. One joins 日 and 月, interpreted as brightness or as dawn with the sun rising while the moon remains. Another, 朙, joins 月 and 囧, a lattice window, to depict moonlight entering a room; 囧 is also proposed as a sound element, though that role is disputed.

components.text: In the 日+月 analysis, 日 depicts the sun in an image associated with brightness or dawn.
In the 日+月 analysis, 月 depicts the moon in an image associated with brightness or dawn.
In 朙, 囧 depicts a lattice window. It is also proposed as a sound element, but the window’s ancient spoken name is not established and the available comparisons do not settle that role.

sound_limitation.text: The proposed sound role remains unresolved. Baxter–Sagart gives different Old Chinese forms for 囧 and 明, while their current Mandarin readings do not establish an ancient correspondence or recover the window’s spoken name.

sound.text: In current Mandarin, 囧 is jiǒng and 明 is míng; this modern comparison does not establish an ancient sound relationship.
In Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese, 囧 is reconstructed as *k-mraŋʔ and 明 as *mraŋ. They differ in initial and final, so this comparison alone does not demonstrate the proposed sound role.

components.text: In 朙, 月 depicts the moon in the interpretation of moonlight entering through a window.

history.text: Sun-and-moon forms are reported in oracle-bone and bronze writing. Other early forms include 朙, analyzed as 月 and 囧, and less secure 目+月 and 田+月 forms. Shuowen identifies 明 as an ancient form of 朙; this historical account does not make 朙 the sole early construction.
A Qin manuscript’s 目-form is reported as a likely graphic corruption of 囧. This proposed change concerns the written form and does not resolve how the distinct early constructions relate.

uncertainties.text: The relative chronology of the early forms and of the dawn and brightness uses is unresolved; exact dates for the cited examples are also unavailable here.

senses.text: Brightness is reported among the uses of oracle-bone examples. The evidence does not show whether this use preceded or followed the attested dawn use.
Dawn is reported among the uses of oracle-bone examples; a Shijing line also illustrates daybreak. Its chronological relation to the brightness sense is unresolved.
Clear or manifest uses are reported in bronze inscriptions. How this sense developed from brightness or dawn is not shown.
Current meanings include bright, light, and clear.

limitations.text: The relative chronology of the early brightness and dawn uses, and the development of later clear or manifest uses, remain unresolved.

overview.text: 明 means “bright” or “clear.” Early writing includes a sun-and-moon form associated with brightness or dawn, and another form, 朙, in which moon and window suggest moonlight entering a room.

components.text: 日 pictures the sun in the early sun-and-moon analysis.
月 pictures the moon in the early sun-and-moon analysis.
In 朙, 囧 pictures a lattice window; its proposed sound role remains uncertain.
In 朙, 月 pictures the moon in the moonlight-through-a-window interpretation.

relationships.text: In the early 日+月 analysis, 日 depicts the sun as part of the celestial image associated with 明.
In the early 日+月 analysis, 月 depicts the moon as part of the celestial image associated with 明.
Shuowen identifies 明 as an ancient form of 朙, whose analysis joins 月 and 囧. This does not show that 朙 was the only early construction.
In 朙, 囧 is described as a lattice window and contributes the window image.
In 朙, 月 depicts the moon in the moonlight-through-a-window interpretation.

囧 is proposed as a sound element in 朙. Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstructions for 囧 (*k-mraŋʔ) and 明 (*mraŋ) differ in initial and final; current Mandarin jiǒng and míng resemble one another but do not settle the historical analysis. The window’s ancient spoken name is not established.
